_note: Template. Copy to <overlay>/config/inference.json and edit. Machine-local backend choice belongs in machine.toml ([inference] backend), not here -- this file is shared across machines via the overlay repo.
_comment_backends: Declared once, referenced by id. oMLX needs Metal and exists only on Apple Silicon; ollama runs anywhere. A machine that cannot run the configured backend names the one it has in machine.toml ([inference] backend = ...), which tools/service-runner.sh exports as SJEL_INFERENCE_BACKEND. That override moves a role only when the role's declared backend is loopback -- a hosted provider answers from every machine -- and only when the role names a model for the target under on_backend.

backends._comment_peer-example: A backend on hardware the operator owns, reached over the tailnet (PRD Q39). provided_by names the systems.local.toml id of the HOST, and trust is the intersection of that name with `owner = "self"` on the same entry -- naming a host is not trusting it, and [nvidia-nim] lives in the same file. tools/lib/external-ref.sh resolves the pair and service-runner.sh exports the result as SJEL_INFERENCE_TRUSTED_PEERS. Without the declaration this backend is an https non-loopback endpoint, which is a cloud provider needing a reviewed policy -- which is exactly what Q39 says a `tailscale cert` peer would wrongly become.

_comment_roles: A role names the backend, the model on it, and that model's input conventions. The prefixes are not decoration: multilingual-e5 expects 'query: ' and 'passage: ', nomic-embed-text expects 'search_query: ' and 'search_document: ', and sending the wrong ones costs retrieval quality without raising anything. Reranking uses the OpenAI-compatible backend's Cohere/Jina-style /rerank endpoint.
_comment_on_backend: What this job is called on another local runtime, keyed by backend id, read only when machine.toml names that backend. A model id is backend-specific, so the name has to travel with the backend or the override just asks Ollama for an MLX model. Prefixes are NOT inherited from the role -- they belong to the model, and this entry names a different one. A role that lists nothing for the machine's backend is unavailable there, which is how reranking behaves on Ollama: the native API has no /rerank at all.

roles._comment_ocr: The `ocr` role EXISTS as a name and is deliberately not declared below. It is rung 3 of the extraction ladder (PRD Q63 -> B30), reached only when rung 2's output trips libs/extraction/src/math.rs, and libs/extraction/src/ocr_role.rs refuses today with or without a declared role. The only way in is a passing record against the frozen DE/EN corpus at libs/extraction/eval/, on unchanged acceptance, reported on the notation verdict line -- the same gate multilingual-e5-base-mlx and bge-reranker-v2-m3-mlx cleared. Apple Vision's baseline there scores 100.0% prose and 58.8% notation, which is why rung 3 is a slot and not a model.
